scope_summary: Prime coat application for bare drywall wall surfaces in new construction. Single prime coat (no finish coats). Assumes drywall is taped, mudded, and sanded by drywall contractor prior to painting scope. Covers all paintable wall field area excluding openings. Does NOT include ceiling prime, wall finish coats, wood/panel walls, or trim prime.
relevant_findings: PVA (polyvinyl acetate) primer is the standard choice for new drywall walls — economical, excellent sealing, water cleanup
Spray+backroll is the NC production standard method. Spray-only is NEVER valid for priming bare drywall — backroll is mandatory to consolidate primer into drywall pores and ensure proper sealing.
18-inch roller is typical for spray+backroll systems but 9-inch is acceptable when obstacles prevent 18-inch use
Single primer coat is standard for NC drywall walls — no need for multiple coats on properly finished drywall
New construction drywall fasteners are mudded and rust-resistant — no spot-priming needed (RC-001)
PVA and acrylic primers are SEALERS, not stain blockers — zero stain blocking capability (RC-002)
Floor protection is conditional on floor_type site condition — subfloor may require no protection (RC-003)
Do not specify dry times in specs — too many variables, refer to PDS (RC-004)
Height modifiers apply to wall tasks when ceiling height creates elevated work areas. An 18ft ceiling means 18ft walls.
Wall prime typically occurs before trim installation (baseboard, casing). Only ceiling edge work matters during prime phase.
Walls and ceilings are typically primed in the same session. Project assembly should optimize shared protection setup/teardown.
When spraying primer on walls and the ceiling is already primed, NO ceiling cut-in is required — spray primer directly into the wall-to-ceiling corner

prep_requirements.method: HEPA vacuum with brush attachment on wall surfaces
prep_requirements.reason: Drywall dust reduces adhesion and causes visible contamination in primer film. Must remove before priming for proper adhesion.

prep_requirements.method: Walk with work light (angled to reveal defects), mark defects for repair
prep_requirements.reason: Identify fastener pops, unfilled joints, damaged paper. Raking light at angles reveals defects that direct light hides.
prep_requirements.skip_conditions: QT2 may reduce to major defects only

prep_requirements.method: Fill defects with joint compound, sand smooth when dry. Use LF heuristic for fastener hole estimation.
prep_requirements.reason: Prime will not hide substrate defects — they must be repaired before priming
prep_requirements.skip_conditions: QT2 addresses major defects only. Drywall repair beyond normal touch-up is drywall contractor responsibility.

limitations: Zero stain blocking — sealer only, not a stain blocker (RC-002)

advantages: Better adhesion and build than PVA

wall_specific_considerations.impact: In spray+backroll systems, backroller sets the pace. Sprayer cannot outrun backroller without causing defects. Spray rate ≤ backroll rate. Use 18" roller when possible to maximize backroll throughput.

18-inch roller is typical for spray+backroll on open areas (primer, ceilings, walls). 9-inch roller is acceptable and may be necessary when obstacles prevent 18-inch use (tight spaces, closets, around fixtures).
Standard 7-8ft ceilings: work from floor. 9-12ft: step ladder for ceiling line cut-in. 13-17ft: extension ladder or scaffold. 18ft+: scaffold or lift.
wall_specific_considerations.rate_adjustment: Height modifiers per Modifier_Registry: H1=1.0 (7-8ft), H2=1.3 (9-12ft), H3=1.5 (13-17ft), H4=2.0 (18ft+)

wall_specific_considerations.consideration: Ceiling edge handling for spray primer
wall_specific_considerations.impact: When spraying primer on walls and the ceiling is already primed, NO cut-in is required at the ceiling line. Spray the primer directly into the wall-to-ceiling corner. Cut-in is only required when: (1) rolling walls, or (2) ceiling is a different finish that must remain clean.
wall_specific_considerations.rate_adjustment: No cut-in task for spray+backroll when ceiling is primed

wall_specific_considerations.impact: Roll method: perimeter floor protection (drops under work area). Spray+backroll: full floor protection (overspray falls to entire floor area). Floor protection is conditional on floor_type — subfloor may need no protection (RC-003).
wall_specific_considerations.rate_adjustment: Protection setup time varies by method and floor type

required_paintscope_keys.required_when: Always — primary quantity driver for wall priming

required_paintscope_keys.description: Linear footage of wall-to-ceiling boundary for edge cut-in
required_paintscope_keys.required_when: When application_method is roll. NOT required for spray+backroll when ceiling is primed.

required_paintscope_keys.description: Perimeter floor protection area for roll method
Full floor protection area for spray overspray
Room count for fixture protection heuristic (avg 6 outlets/switches per room)
Floor area for post-prime vacuum cleanup

zones_required.rationale: Spray creates overspray that falls to floor. Full floor coverage required when spraying walls.
Roll method has minimal drip risk — perimeter drops sufficient under work area.
Electrical outlets, switches, and any installed fixtures need protection from overspray.

protection_zones_analysis.conditional_protection_note: Floor protection is conditional on floor_type site condition per RC-003. Subfloor (typical NC sequence) may require no floor protection. Finished/partial floors require full protection regime.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: When working on walls, we do NOT mask off drywall ceilings. We either cut in at the ceiling line (roll method) or spray directly into the corner (spray method when ceiling is primed). Ceiling masking is only required for millwork ceilings.
adjacent_surfaces.affected_tasks: Cut-in at ceiling line (roll method only)

adjacent_surfaces.notes: In NC sequence, baseboard is typically NOT installed during wall prime phase. This adjacency is declared for project-level tracking but does NOT create edge work tasks in this spec.
adjacent_surfaces.affected_tasks: None during prime phase (baseboard not installed)

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Door casing is typically NOT installed during wall prime phase in NC. Declared for completeness.
adjacent_surfaces.affected_tasks: None during prime phase (casing not installed)

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Window casing is typically NOT installed during wall prime phase in NC. Declared for completeness.
adjacent_surfaces.affected_tasks: None during prime phase (casing not installed)

conditions_affecting_tasks.impact: Determines floor protection requirements. Finished floors require full protection. Subfloor may require no protection (RC-003).
Ceiling height determines access equipment for ceiling-line cut-in. Higher walls require ladder/scaffold work.
conditions_affecting_tasks.affects_tasks: Cut-in task, possibly rolling near ceiling line

conditions_affecting_tasks.impact: When ceiling is primed and walls are being spray primed, no cut-in is required — spray directly into corner. When rolling walls, cut-in is always required regardless of ceiling state.
conditions_affecting_tasks.affects_tasks: Cut-in task conditional on application method and ceiling state

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: For roll method: cut-in required at ceiling line. For spray method when ceiling is primed: NO cut-in — spray into corner. We do NOT mask drywall ceilings when working on walls.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Drywall ceilings are never masked when working on walls. Cut in or spray into corner. Only millwork ceilings would require masking.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Baseboard is typically NOT installed during prime phase in NC. No edge work required at this boundary during wall prime.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Baseboard installed after prime, before or after finish. Not a prime-phase concern.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Door casing is typically NOT installed during prime phase in NC. No edge work required.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Door casing installed after prime. Not a prime-phase concern.

adjacency_notes.scope_impact: Window casing is typically NOT installed during prime phase in NC. No edge work required.
adjacency_notes.nc_context: Window casing installed after prime. Not a prime-phase concern.

valid_input_states.rationale: NC wall prime spec operates only on bare drywall. Cannot prime already-primed walls. If wall is already primed (SS_PRIMED), this spec does not apply.

output_state.rationale: Wall prime leaves surface in field-primed state, ready for finish coats. This is distinct from factory-primed (SS_PRIMED_FACTORY) which applies to millwork.

adjacent_state_protection_analysis.rationale: We do NOT mask drywall ceilings when working on walls, regardless of ceiling state. We cut in at the ceiling line (roll) or spray directly into the corner (spray when ceiling is primed). Only millwork ceilings would require masking.
Baseboard is typically NOT installed during wall prime in NC. If present and finished (rare), light mask at wall-baseboard junction.

notes_for_materials_manager: PVA primer for QT2-QT3, acrylic latex for QT4, high-build for Level 5
Coverage rates are standard drywall primer rates (~300-400 SF/gal depending on drywall finish level and texture)
Level 3 drywall has higher absorption — reduce coverage rate
Level 5 drywall may require high-build primer for uniform sheen
Spray tip selection: 517 typical for drywall primer (larger than finish tips)
Roller nap selection: 3/8" to 1/2" for smooth drywall, 1/2" for orange peel and knockdown. Do NOT use 3/4" for knockdown — 3/4" is only for stomp/popcorn texture or porous masonry.
18-inch roller typical for spray+backroll, 9-inch acceptable when obstacles prevent 18-inch
Floor protection materials: rosin paper for hard floors (spray), drops for roll method
PVA primer is SEALER only — no stain blocking claims (RC-002)
notes_for_sop_librarian: Use TSK_WALL_* prefix for wall prime task IDs (distinct from TSK_CEIL_* ceiling tasks)
Vacuum step is CRITICAL — dust removal before priming is mandatory
No spot-prime tasks for fasteners (RC-001 — fasteners are mudded by drywall contractor)
Spray+backroll coupling constraint: backroller sets pace, spray rate ≤ backroll rate
Edge cut-in at ceiling line is conditional: required for roll method, NOT required for spray+backroll when ceiling is primed
Do NOT include ceiling masking task — we cut in or spray into corner, never mask drywall ceilings
Floor protection: perimeter for roll, full room for spray_backroll (conditional on floor_type)
Fixture protection (outlet covers) for spray methods only
Inspection/repair intensity driven by quality_tier — not application quality
notes_for_estimation_engineer: Wall prime has independent researched rates — do not derive from other specs
Roll rates: ~350-400 SF/hr smooth drywall, ~275-325 SF/hr textured drywall
Spray rates: ~600-700 SF/hr (but coupled to backroll rate in spray_backroll method)
Backroll rates: ~400-500 SF/hr — this is the effective spray+backroll system rate
Cut-in rates: ~100-120 LF/hr at ceiling line (standard height) — only for roll method
Height modifiers per Modifier_Registry: H1=1.0 (7-8ft), H2=1.3 (9-12ft), H3=1.5 (13-17ft), H4=2.0 (18ft+)
QT modifiers for inspection/repair intensity: QT2=0.8, QT3=1.0, QT4=1.3
Floor protection setup varies by method and floor_type — budget more time for spray protection
Use LF heuristic for fastener hole estimation (standard)
assumptions: All drywall is standard gypsum board (not specialized types)
New construction surface condition is 'Good' — minimal defects expected from drywall contractor
Standard ceiling height 7-8 ft is baseline; height modifiers apply above that
Drywall contractor has completed all taping, mudding, and sanding prior to paint scope
Walls and ceilings are typically primed in the same session in NC production
Trim (baseboard, door casing, window casing) is NOT installed during wall prime phase
Floor type varies — site condition determines protection requirements
Drywall ceilings are never masked when working on walls
uncertainties: Exact coverage rate reduction for Level 3 vs Level 4 drywall finish — needs field validation
Fixture count heuristic (6 per room) — may vary significantly by house design
Production rate ranges will be calibrated through actual job data over time

qt2_scope_analysis.summary: QT2 for NC drywall wall prime means reduced prep intensity with unchanged application quality. Inspection is quick walk-through (major defects only). Dust removal is a quick pass. Cut-in edge standards are relaxed (acceptable wobble if coverage complete). Final inspection is a quick visual scan. Application quality is NOT reduced — drips, sags, and holidays still fail at QT2.
included_tasks: TSK_WALL_ROLL_PRIMER / TSK_WALL_SPRAY_PRIMER / TSK_WALL_BACKROLL_PRIMER (binary - same at all tiers)
TSK_WALL_CUT_IN_CEILING (at reduced precision standard) — roll method only
All protection tasks (binary - same at all tiers)

reduced_tasks.qt2_behavior: Quick walk-through, major defects only (fastener pops, holes, unfilled joints)
reduced_tasks.qt2_rate: Faster than QT3 baseline due to reduced scrutiny

reduced_tasks.qt2_behavior: Quick pass to remove loose dust
reduced_tasks.qt2_rate: Same rate but less thorough coverage

reduced_tasks.qt2_behavior: Acceptable edge, coverage priority over line quality. Minor wavering tolerated.
reduced_tasks.qt2_rate: Faster than QT3 due to relaxed precision standard

reduced_tasks.qt2_behavior: Quick visual scan for major misses. No raking light.

inspection_standard.lighting: ambient (no raking light required at QT2)
inspection_standard.notes: Quick visual walk-through. Only flag obvious defects visible at 6ft in ambient light.

acceptable: Minor edge wobble on cut-in lines (if coverage is complete)
Small ridges and dimples not addressed
Visible edge imperfections at close distance
unacceptable: Major unfilled defects (holes, unfilled joints, exposed fasteners)

disclaimers: QT2 is for economy/rental grade work only
Surface eligibility: NC bare drywall qualifies by default (no putty knife test needed)
Profile tolerance 1/8 inch for existing surfaces (N/A for bare NC drywall)
Sheen limited to flat/eggshell for QT2 finish coats
Application quality is NOT reduced at QT2 - only prep and inspection intensity
Drips, sags, holidays, and lap marks fail at ALL quality tiers including QT2
qt2_scope_analysis.nc_specific_notes: For NC bare drywall walls, QT2 eligibility is automatic. The QT2 scope reduction applies to inspection intensity and edge precision only. Primer application must still properly seal the drywall at all tiers.

cross_spec_coordination.impact: If inspection/repair is performed during wall prime, SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH should check this flag and reduce or eliminate its first inspection/repair round to avoid double-counting labor.
